IBPS PO Notification 2026: Your Gateway to a Promising Banking Career!

The highly anticipated IBPS PO Notification 2026 (CRP-XVI PO/MT) has officially been released by the Institute of Banking Personnel Selection, marking a significant opportunity for aspiring banking professionals across India. With 6715 Probationary Officer vacancies announced across 11 participating public sector banks, this year's recruitment drive promises a robust chance to embark on a fulfilling career.

The online application process is currently live, inviting eligible graduates to apply and take their first step towards becoming a Probationary Officer. Read on for a comprehensive breakdown of important dates, eligibility, the updated exam pattern, and how to successfully navigate the application process.

Key Highlights of IBPS PO 2026 Notification

✅ Official Notification Released: The IBPS PO 2026 notification (CRP-XVI PO/MT) was released on July 1, 2026.

✅ Significant Vacancies: A total of 6715 Probationary Officer/Management Trainee posts are available across 11 Public Sector Banks.

✅ Online Application Live: The application window opened on July 1, 2026.

✅ Revised Mains Exam Pattern: This year sees an increased question count and specific distribution for the objective Mains exam.

✅ Three-Stage Selection: The recruitment process includes Preliminary Exam, Main Exam, and Interview.

Important Dates for IBPS PO 2026

Stay on top of your application and preparation with these crucial dates:

Activity Tentative Schedule
IBPS PO Notification 2026 Release Date July 1, 2026
Online Registration & Application Fee Payment July 1, 2026 – July 21, 2026
Pre-Examination Training (PET) Call Letter August 2026
Conduct of Pre-Examination Training (PET) August 2026
Download of Call Letters for Online Preliminary Exam August 2026
Online Preliminary Examination August 22 & 23, 2026 (tentative)
Result of Online Preliminary Examination September 2026
Download of Call Letters for Online Main Examination September/October 2026
Online Main Examination October 4, 2026 (tentative)
Declaration of Result – Main Examination November 2026
Personality Test / Conduct of Interview November/December 2026 – January 2027
Provisional Allotment January/February 2027

Note: While some sources indicate August 2025 dates for a previous cycle's prelims, the most recent IBPS Calendar 2026 confirms prelims on August 22 & 23, 2026, and Mains on October 4, 2026.

IBPS PO 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Before applying, ensure you meet the essential eligibility requirements:

1. Nationality
Candidates must be either an Indian Citizen, a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, a Tibetan refugee who settled in India before January 1, 1962, or a person of Indian origin who has migrated from specific countries with the intention of permanently settling in India. Those in the last three categories require a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India.
2. Age Limit (as of July 1, 2026)
Applicants must be between 20 and 30 years old. This means a candidate must have been born not earlier than 02.07.1996 and not later than 01.07.2006 (both dates inclusive). Age relaxations are applicable for reserved categories (e.g., SC/ST, OBC, PwBD) as per government norms.
3. Educational Qualification (as of July 21, 2026)
A Graduation Degree in any discipline from a university recognized by the Government of India or an equivalent qualification is mandatory. Candidates must possess a valid mark sheet/degree certificate proving they are a graduate on or before the registration day (July 21, 2026) and must indicate their percentage of marks while applying online.

IBPS PO 2026 Exam Pattern: What's New?

The IBPS PO selection process comprises three distinct phases: Preliminary Exam, Main Exam, and Interview. Understanding the exam pattern is crucial for effective preparation.

1. Preliminary Examination
This is an online, objective test of 1-hour duration, carrying a total of 100 marks for 100 questions. It's a qualifying stage.
  • Sections: English Language, Reasoning Ability, Quantitative Aptitude.
  • Negative Marking: 0.25 marks deducted for each incorrect answer.
  • Candidates must qualify in each of the three tests by securing minimum cut-off marks.
2. Main Examination
The Mains exam is more comprehensive, consisting of both Objective and Descriptive tests, conducted online. The marks obtained in the Main Examination will be considered for shortlisting for interviews and for final merit listing.
  • Objective Test: Total 200 marks, 170 questions. Duration: 3 hours.
    • Reasoning & Computer Aptitude: 40 Questions, 60 Marks, 60 minutes.
    • General/Economy/Banking Awareness: 50 Questions, 50 Marks, 35 minutes (includes Digital/Financial Awareness and RBI circulars).
    • English Language: 40 Questions, 40 Marks, 40 minutes.
    • Data Analysis & Interpretation: 40 Questions, 60 Marks, 45 minutes.
  • Descriptive Test: Total 25 marks, 2 questions (Essay and Letter Writing). Duration: 30 minutes. Topics may be broadly based on Economic and Social issues, emerging trends in Banking and Technology, Current events, Ethics.
  • Negative Marking: 0.25 marks deducted for each wrong answer in the objective test.
3. Interview
Candidates who clear the Mains examination will be called for a Personal Interview, conducted by the participating banks and coordinated by the Nodal Bank. This round carries a maximum of 100 marks, and candidates need to score at least 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PWD) to qualify. A non-qualifying Personality Test may also be included before the interviews.

How to Apply for IBPS PO 2026

The application process is entirely online. Follow these steps to ensure a smooth submission:

✅ Visit the official IBPS website: www.ibps.in.

✅ Click on "CRP PO/MT" and then "Click here to Apply Online for Common Recruitment Process for Probationary Officers/Management Trainee-XVI".

✅ Register as a new candidate by providing basic details to generate a provisional registration ID and password.

✅ Fill in the detailed application form, including personal and educational qualifications.

✅ Upload required documents: scanned photograph, signature, left thumb impression, and a handwritten declaration. A live photograph capture may also be required.

✅ Pay the application fee online through debit/credit card, net banking, UPI, or mobile wallets.

✅ Review your application carefully before final submission and print a copy for your records.

It is advisable to apply well before the closing date (July 21, 2026) to avoid any last-minute technical glitches due to heavy website traffic.

Why Choose a Career as an IBPS PO?

Becoming a Probationary Officer in a Public Sector Bank is more than just a job; it's a stable and respected career path with immense growth potential. Here's why you should consider it:

Job Security and Prestige
Public Sector Bank jobs offer unparalleled job security and are highly regarded in Indian society.
Attractive Salary & Benefits
IBPS POs receive a competitive salary package, along with various allowances and benefits like medical aid, housing, and provident fund.
Career Growth
Banks provide excellent opportunities for promotion and professional development, allowing you to climb the corporate ladder within the banking sector.
Learning and Development
The role of a PO offers exposure to diverse banking operations, fostering continuous learning and skill enhancement.

The IBPS PO 2026 notification is a golden opportunity for graduates aspiring to make a mark in the banking sector. With significant vacancies and a clear recruitment roadmap, now is the time to dedicate yourself to preparation. Stay informed, prepare diligently, and seize this chance to build a successful career with one of India's leading public sector banks. Good luck!
